hypothesis: We believe the HDD skill produces actionable hypotheses from messy real-world artifacts if practitioners submit PRDs, decks, and briefs and can get clear next steps (INK → PRE → test plan).
baseline: No baseline — this is the first test of the skill on real artifacts.
success_threshold: ≥3 of 5 test artifacts yield ≥1 hypothesis that the submitter confirms is more actionable than what they had before analysis
falsification_criteria: This hypothesis is FALSE if: (1) <3 of 5 artifacts yield actionable output, (2) users say they could have done this themselves without the skill, (3) generated hypotheses lack situation/motivation/outcome structure
outcome_notes: THRESHOLD MET: 5/5. Every artifact produced more specific testable output than existed before. Intake surfaced gaps invisible to original authors. LEARNING: Skill's weakest phase is Phase 5 output routing. Input contract catches structural gaps; output contract doesn't evaluate experiment design quality. NEXT: PRE-003.

hypothesis: We believe distinguishable frustration patterns are achievable if workers with daily AI tool use can get compared meaningfully to workers with minimal AI exposure using self-reported journal entries.
baseline: No baseline — pilot required to establish whether cohort-specific themes emerge at all.
success_threshold: Cohen's kappa ≥0.6 on cohort-specific frustration theme coding across two independent raters
falsification_criteria: This hypothesis is FALSE if: (1) Qualitative coding finds no consistent theme separation between AI-Heavy and Low-AI cohorts after N≥30 entries per cohort, (2) Inter-rater agreement on cohort assignment from blind journal review is no better than chance (κ<0.2), (3) Participants in AI-Heavy cohort cannot name specific tools or describe daily AI workflows when asked in follow-up
timeline: Pilot: 5 participants/cohort × 7 days. Full study contingent on pilot results.

hypothesis: We believe the skill's output contract can enforce experiment design validity if teams generating hypotheses can get explicit challenge criteria for whether their proposed test method actually isolates the variable under test.
baseline: No baseline — current output contract accepts any test method that has a stopping condition.
success_threshold: ≥80% of generated hypotheses include explicit confound acknowledgment or controlled design when test method involves correlation claims
falsification_criteria: This hypothesis is FALSE if: (1) Adding validity checks causes >50% of hypothesis generation attempts to stall without resolution, (2) Practitioners say the challenge criteria feel like bureaucracy rather than clarification, (3) Well-designed experiments get flagged as invalid due to false positive triggers

hypothesis: We believe an effort forecast built by resampling a team's own past forecast errors (Monte Carlo over the ratio of actual to forecast) gives ranges a team can plan with, unlike a range built by adding up every part's best and worst case. Tested forward in time on TerraQuotes' delivery ledger: each issue is forecast using only the issues finished before it.
primary_metric: Forward-in-time coverage and median width (high ÷ low) of the 80% range
baseline: per issue and per batch of 10 issues
success_threshold: TerraQuotes' current forecaster adds each cost term's low and high cases. On its 117 measured issues as of 2026-10-29, 55% of actuals fall inside its range, and the range is about 16 times wider at the top than at the bottom. The forward-in-time Monte Carlo backtest has not been run; only a leave-one-out version, on 50 issues, has been looked at.
falsification_criteria: The 80% range covers 70% to 90% of actuals per issue
timeline: and its median width is under half the current tool's
status: This is false if, forward in time: (1) the 80% range covers under 70% or over 90% of actuals; (2) its median width is not under half the current tool's; or (3) for batches of 10 issues, coverage falls outside 70% to 90%. With fewer than 30 issues that have earlier issues to learn from, we can't tell.
outcome_logged_at: One backtest when the forecaster lands
outcome_notes: then again each time 20 more issues are measured

hypothesis: We believe a range read straight from a team's own past misses, interpolating between them at the (n+1) positions in log space, covers about 80% of actuals at every history size from ten items up. The current forecaster's 4,000 resampled draws cover only about 70% to 77% of actuals when a team has 10 to 30 finished items, because a bootstrap of a short history under-reaches its tails. That made the README's trust rule ("coverage should sit near 0.8") raise false alarms for exactly the teams just starting.  Chosen after an exploratory simulation, run before this prediction, which compared five methods on lognormal, heavy-tailed and TerraQuotes-resampled histories of 9 to 100 items. This prediction is tested on a fresh simulation (a seed not used in that exploration) and on the real TerraQuotes ledger, which has not been run with this method.
primary_metric: Coverage of the 80% range: (a) in a fresh simulation
baseline: by history size; (b) forward in time on TerraQuotes' 146 measured issues
falsification_criteria: The current forecaster (PRE-004): forward in time on TerraQuotes, 131 forecasts, 79% coverage, median width 7.07. In simulation with 10 to 30 finished items it covers 68% to 79%.
timeline: (a) Coverage between 77% and 85% at each history size of 10
column13: in each of the three simulated histories; (b) on TerraQuotes
column16: This is false if: (1) at any of those history sizes, in any of the three simulated histories, coverage falls outside 77% to 85%; (2) on TerraQuotes, coverage falls outside 75% to 85%; or (3) the median width on TerraQuotes is 9 or more, which would mean the fix bought its coverage by giving up the planning value of the range.
column18: when the change lands; the TerraQuotes check reruns with PRE-004's
